newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Yanhua shares seen weak on debut.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Yanhua shares seen weak on debut.

text.p: Concern over the volatile profitability of petrochemical industry in China is seen hurting performance of the H-shares of Beijing Yanhua Petrochemical Co Ltd on their first day of trading on Wednesday, analysts said.
"The company's earnings is hard to predict when its profitability is exposed to the volatile petrochemical products and crude oil prices," said Pamela Lam, analyst at Pacific Challenge Securities.
Analysts said the recent weak market towards H-shares might also dampen investors' interest in the stock.
"The recent market focus was mainly on the red-chips and that trimmed demand for H-shares," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
H-shares are shares of China-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong, while red chips are Hong Kong-based companies with Chinese backing.
Analysts said hope of asset injection among red-chips had fuelled strong buying interest for the sector, and that had left the H-shares sector unattended.

Beijing Yanhua issued 1.012 billion new H-shares, or 30 percent of its enlarged share capital, in a global offering of the company's shares. H-shares are shares of Chinese incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong.

Of the total shares issued, 455.4 million shares were offered to the U.S. market in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADS). Another 455.4 million shares are for international placement with the balance for public subscription in Hong Kong. The issue price of the Beijing Yanhua shares had been fixed at HK$1.78 per share.

Analysts said the subscription response for the issue was also seen to be cool with the international placement portion a few times subscribed and the Hong Kong offering tranche of slightly more than 10 times subscribed.
The Chinese resins and plastics producer is due to make an official statement on its subscription results on Tuesday.
"Its short term earnings outlook is seen unexciting when the company will use a substantial portion of the proceeds to repay debt," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
Beijing Yanhua had said the net proceeds to be raised from the issue would be used to repay outstanding bank borrowings with the balance to fund expansion of existing production facilities.
However, some analysts said the company earnings potential was seen bright in the long run due to an increasing demand for resins and plastics in China.
